diagnostic_evidence.quote: Wahba's problem aims at finding a nonzero quaternion $\qq$ that minimizes the cost function
The presented results offer a complete theoretical characterisation of the Wahba problem in quaternions
Then, \eqref{eq:WAHBAS_EQUATION} has a solution if and only if $(\qa[1],\qa[2]) \sim (\qb[1], \qb[2])$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines Wahba's problem as minimizing f(q), and the intro/conclusion claim to solve it and to give a complete characterisation. The formal results only characterise the set where f(q)=0, which exists only when the data are exactly pairwise similar (noise-free). For generic (noisy) observations no zero exists and the paper gives no minimizer; the minimization problem for l=2 is not solved.

failure_location.quote: In this paper, we solve the Wahba's problem for the special and practically important case $\ell = 2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the introductory and concluding claims to the zero-cost case f(q)=0 for exactly pairwise similar observations, as the abstract already does.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope (solving/completely characterising Wahba's problem for two observations) exceeds what is established; only the consistent zero-cost case is covered.
issues.title: Prose claims to solve Wahba's minimization problem, but only the zero-cost (consistent-data) case is treated
issues.why_classification: Repair is textual, but it withdraws the promise of solving the minimization problem; the formal content is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Substituting \eqref{eq:PAIRWISE_SIMILARITY_PROOF_PART_1} into \eqref{eq:SUM_SIMILARITY} yields $\qq[][-1]\qa[2]\qq[] = \qb[2]$, which completes the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: The q in (SUM_SIMILARITY) is a specific quaternion conjugating a1+a2 to b1+b2. The proof then redefines q := q1 q2 with q2 commuting with b1 so that q conjugates a1 to b1, and substitutes into (SUM_SIMILARITY) as if it were the same q. Nothing shows that the two 2-dimensional solution sets {q: q^{-1}a1 q=b1} and {q: q^{-1}(a1+a2)q=b1+b2} intersect nontrivially; the converse direction is therefore unproved. (Also, similarity of a1+a2 and b1+b2 is invoked without checking a1+a2 is nonreal, as Definition 2.3 requires.)

failure_location.quote: Assume that $\qq[1]$ is a nonzero quaternion with $\qq[1][-1]\qa[1]\qq[1]=\qb[1]$. Set $\qq = \qq[1]\qq[2]$, where $\qq[2]$ is a nonzero quaternion such that $\qb[1]\qq[2] = \qq[2]\qb[1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the converse argument by a direct one: equal norms and equal inner products of Im a1, Im a2 and Im b1, Im b2 (which follow from the hypotheses) imply existence of a rotation, hence a unit quaternion p, mapping both imaginary parts simultaneously; handle the case of a real sum separately.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if' direction of the lemma lacks a valid proof; the statement itself is true (two vector pairs with equal Gram matrices are related by a rotation), and downstream results use only the 'only if' direction.
issues.title: Converse of pairwise-similarity characterization: proof conflates two different conjugating quaternions
issues.why_classification: The result survives, but a replacement (contained, nontrivial) argument is needed rather than a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\qq$ be a solution of \eqref{eq:WAHBAS_EQUATION}. Then, it holds
and hence \eqref{eq:HOMOGENEOUS_WAHBAS_EQUATION_PERPENDICULAR_COMPONENTS}, which completes the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts equivalence, but the proof starts from a solution q of (WAHBAS_EQUATION) and derives q^{-1}(a1×a2)q=b1×b2, i.e. only that (HOMOGENEOUS_WAHBAS_EQUATION_PERPENDICULAR_COMPONENTS) is necessary. The converse (that q^{-1}a1q=b1 and q^{-1}(a1×a2)q=b1×b2 imply q^{-1}a2q=b2) is a nontrivial step requiring the orthogonal-frame decomposition of Im a2 in {Im a1, Im a1×Im a2, Im a1×(Im a1×Im a2)} together with the pairwise-similarity conditions, and a separate treatment of the parallel case Im a1×Im a2=0; none of this is given. Theorem 4.7 relies on the equivalence to conclude that its parametrization consists of solutions of (WAHBAS_EQUATION).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the converse argument: a rotation fixing Im a1 -> Im b1 and Im a1×Im a2 -> Im b1×Im b2 also maps Im a1×(Im a1×Im a2) correctly, and the coordinates of Im a2 and Im b2 in these frames coincide by pairwise similarity; treat Im a1 parallel Im a2 separately.
issues.overall_effect: Without the converse, the set derived in Theorem 4.7 is only known to contain all solutions, not to consist of solutions; the lemma's equivalence (and hence the theorem's soundness) is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Equivalence with the perpendicular-components equation: only necessity is proved
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and the method survives, but a contained nontrivial argument must be supplied for a direction the main theorem depends on.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, multiplying \eqref{eq:HOMOGENEOUS_SOLUTION_PROOF_PART_2} by $\qq[2]$ from the left yields $\qa[3]\qq[2] -\qq[2]\qb[3] = 0$ such that by Theorem~\ref{theorem:NONZERO_SOLUTIONS_OF_THE_HOMOGENEOUS_SYLVESTER_EQUATION}

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses allow Im a1 parallel to Im a2 (e.g. a1=a2=b1=b2=i, which are nonreal and pairwise similar). Then a3=b3=0 are real, so Theorem 3.3 (stated for similar, hence nonreal, quaternions) is applied outside its hypotheses, and the square root in (Q2) is of 0, which Lemma 3.1 excludes; the natural value gives q2=0 and q=0, not a solution, whereas the true solution set is q=q1 for any q1 in (Q1) (a 2-parameter family). The stated 'general solution' is thus wrong/ill-defined in this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis Im a1 × Im a2 ≠ 0 to Theorem 4.7 (and state separately that for parallel observations the solution set is q = q1 from (Q1)).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4.7's parametrization fails for parallel (collinear) observation pairs; the nondegenerate case is unaffected.
issues.title: Main solution theorem breaks down for parallel observations (Im a1 × Im a2 = 0)
issues.why_classification: A degenerate case is excluded by a standard local hypothesis with a trivially described solution; conclusion and method survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\qp$ is either an arbitrary pure quaternion if $\qa$ is a negative real

issues.failure_explanation: In the case a3 = -b3, sqrt(a3 b3*) is an arbitrary pure quaternion (Lemma 3.1), and the proof's computation of q2 b1 - b1 q2 silently drops the λ2 term, which only vanishes if the chosen root commutes with b1. The theorem's constraint only requires Im q2 ⊥ a3, which does not force q2 ∈ span{1,b1}. Counterexample: a1=b1=i, a2=j, b2=-j (pairwise similar), q1=1, a3=k=-b3; the theorem admits q2=j (pure, ⊥ k), but q=j gives j^{-1} i j = -i ≠ b1, so f(q)≠0. The correct requirement is q2 = λ2 Im b1. In addition, the degenerate condition is written with q1* rather than q1^{-1}, so q1*(...)q1 has norm |q1|^2|Im a1×Im a2| and the stated trigger can only fire when |q1|=1, although the square-root ambiguity arises for every q1 in that geometric case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second constraint by: if q1^{-1}(Im a1×Im a2)q1 = -(Im b1×Im b2), then q2 = λ2 Im b1 (equivalently Im q2 parallel to Im b1); correct the proof by keeping the λ2 term and using that the root must commute with b1.
issues.overall_effect: In the antiparallel degenerate case (the needed rotation of a3 is by π), the theorem's 'general solution' set contains quaternions that are not solutions of (WAHBAS_EQUATION), and the case condition is mis-specified; the nondegenerate case is correct.
issues.title: Degenerate antiparallel case: stated constraint on q2 admits non-solutions and is scaled inconsistently
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a degenerate case restores the theorem; the generic closed-form solution and method are unchanged.
